item.title: [SwiftHFR] Alertes Qualitay: a new alert is spoken as « Nouvelle », a seen one is regular (#1160)
item.body:
Closes #1160
Claim: cloud/m4q-small-sonnet
Author model: Sonnet 5.5 (cloud/m4q-small-sonnet)

**Problem.** In Alertes Qualitay a new alert differs from a seen one by weight and grey only; VoiceOver hears no state (HIG › VoiceOver, › Accessibility).

**Cause.** `QualityAlertRow` combined its children without an accessibility value; the weight step was semibold→bold.

**Change.** `Row.accessibilityState` (« Nouvelle » when new, empty otherwise) applied with `.accessibilityValue` on the combined row; `Row.titleStyle` (headline when new, body when seen: same size, regular instead of semibold, as legacy `AQPlusView.swift:405-407` @ 87fe0d1c). Nothing else touched.

**Tests.** `QualityAlertsModelTests` (captured feed, 2 new rows): the state is spoken for exactly the new rows and the style follows `isNew` (fail without the change: no such members). Cloud session: not built here (no Xcode), compile-check requested; VoiceOver check on the next device review (#893).

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, cloud/r1160-opus-review, round 1): REQUEST CHANGES** (head c1ae0852)

1. **Medium**, `App/SwiftHFRTests/QualityAlerts/QualityAlertsModelTests.swift:46-49`. The test only checks the model's `accessibilityState` string. #1160's check asks for "a hosted test on the row's accessibility value". If you delete `.accessibilityValue(row.accessibilityState)` in `QualityAlertsView.swift:117`, the defect comes back and every test stays green (L01). The view wiring is where the risk sits: a row with a `target` is wrapped in `Button(action:) { content }`, so VoiceOver reads the Button, while the value is set on a combined element inside the Button's label. No existing precedent shows that path: `LegacyTopicRowView:52` puts it on a list row with a tag, not inside a Button. **Fix:** add a hosted test using `HostedAccessibility.elements(under:)`, as `ListLookHostedTests` and `FavorisHeaderTapHostedTests` do. It should host the list with one new row and one seen row, both with a target, and expect `accessibilityValue == "Nouvelle"` on the first and an empty value on the second. If the value does not reach the Button, move `.accessibilityValue` onto the `Button`.
2. **Low**, `QualityAlertsModelTests.swift:49`. The `titleStyle` expectation is the same `isNew ? .headline : .body` expression copied from the code, so it is a tautology. It cannot catch a wrong style choice. **Fix:** assert concrete values on known rows (row 0 is new, so `.headline`; a seen row, so `.body`), or drop it.
3. **Detail**, `QualityAlertsView.swift:4-8`. The "Differences:" pointer does not mention the spoken « Nouvelle », which legacy lacks (`AQPlusView.swift:405-407` has no accessibility text). Add it, naming #1160.

Points checked and correct:
- Legacy pointer: `87fe0d1c:AQPlusView.swift:405-407` is `titleFont: .headline`, `titleWeight: item.isNew ? .bold : .regular`.
- Body and headline are the same size: `TextScale.pointSize` reads `UIFont.preferredFont`, and Apple's table gives body and headline the same size at every Dynamic Type category. So `.body` regular for a seen row matches legacy's regular headline, and a new row is semibold plus `.bold` = bold.
- Types and imports: `Font.TextStyle` is Hashable, and the test file imports SwiftUI.
- No added line goes past 140 columns.

**Checked:** I read the diff, the issue #1160 body, `TextScale.swift`, `LegacyTopicRowView.swift` and the legacy `87fe0d1c` lines, searched for hosted accessibility helpers, and measured line lengths. I did not build or run tests: there is no Xcode here and no worktree was created.

Round 1 fixed in 2d7d758 (hosted test `QualityAlertRowHostedTests`, concrete style expectations, pointer). Round 2 requested.

**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, cloud/r1160-opus-r2, round 2): REQUEST CHANGES** — head 2d7d75816c7e5135c66cc669241c72b5b7d2a6ad

1. **High** — `App/SwiftHFRTests/QualityAlerts/QualityAlertRowHostedTests.swift:36-39`. This test fails every time, whether or not the fix is there. `Support.model(source:)` uses an empty `InMemorySettingsStore`, so `aqLastCheck` is unset and `lastCheck` falls back to `QualityAlertsModel.neverChecked` (2010-01-01, `QualityAlertsModel.swift:81,119`). All 25 items in T01 have a date (`AQParsersTests.swift:72` requires `publishedAt` for each one), all dated 2025–2026. `AQClient.isNew` is `publishedAt >= lastCheck`, so all 25 rows are new and `#require(model.rows.first(where: { !$0.isNew && … }))` throws before any accessibility check runs. The test therefore proves nothing in either direction (LESSONS L01), and it would turn the app-test job red. **Fix:** pass a store seeded with `Support.lastCheckOfTheOracle`, as `showingTheListMarksItSeenAndClearsTheBadge` does. That gives 2 new rows and 23 seen ones. Then check that both chosen rows have `target != nil`.
2. **Medium** (open until 1 is fixed and the test runs green on CI) — `QualityAlertsView.swift:116-117`. The value sits on the combined `content`, inside `Button(action:open).buttonStyle(.plain)`. It is not proven that the Button's merged element exposes the inner element's `accessibilityValue`. Nothing else in the app uses this layout under test: `LegacyTopicRowView:52` puts it on a combined row that is not inside a Button. The search in the test (an element whose label contains the title, with value "Nouvelle") is the right check, and without `.accessibilityValue` the new-row expectation goes red. If it stays red with the modifier in place, move `.accessibilityValue(row.accessibilityState)` onto the `Button` (and keep it on `content` for the branch without a target).

Fixed since round 1: the `titleStyle` assertion now checks the real value (`.headline` for a new row, `.body` for a seen one), and the Differences pointer names the spoken « Nouvelle ».

**Verified:** I read the diff at the head; went through `HostedAccessibility` (begin/endAutomation paired, `elements(under:)`, same usage as `ListLookHostedTests`); checked that `QualityAlertRow` is internal, its memberwise init and trailing `open`, and `Row.target`; followed the `isNew` chain (`lastCheck` → `neverChecked` → `AQClient.isNew`) and the T01 pubDates (25 of 25 dated). `swiftlint lint --strict` on the 4 changed files: 0 violations. No Xcode, so I did not run the hosted test.

**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, cloud/r1160-opus-review, round 3) : APPROVE** — head 301738a

The round 2 findings are resolved:
- **Seeding**: `Support.lastCheckOfTheOracle` is 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC. Only the first two items of `T01` are newer, and both are `forum2.php?…cat=13…` links, so both get a target. Of the 23 seen rows, 21 are `forum2.php` links and 2 are `sujet_…htm` links. So both `#require`s succeed.
- **Imports**: `InMemorySettingsStore` and `SettingKey.aqLastCheck` come from `HFRStorage`, which the test imports. The `SwiftUI` import added to the model tests is needed for `Font.TextStyle ==`.
- **Spec #1160**: the diff gives « Nouvelle » and a regular weight for seen rows (`.body` gives `.regular` through `TextScale.font`; a new row gets `.headline` + `.bold`).
- **Button / value**: the inner `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` keeps the explicit value; a `.plain` `Button` merges its label's element, values included. No existing test proves this, but `aNewRowIsSpokenAsNewAndASeenOneIsNot` checks it on the real tree, fails without the change, and cannot pass on an empty tree. Do not add the value to the `Button` as well (it could be read twice). If the test fails on CI, move the modifier to the `Button` and keep it on the branch without a target.

Findings:
1. **Low** — `QualityAlertRowHostedTests.swift:29`: the filter matches any element whose label contains the title; if SwiftUI exposed the inner element and the button separately, the test could pass on the inner one. Suggested fix: also check that a matched element has `.button` in `accessibilityTraits`. Not blocking.

**Checked**: full diff; dates and links of `T01` recomputed; `QualityAlertsModel.load`/`target`, `TextScale.font`, `HostedAccessibility`; `swiftlint lint --strict` on the 4 changed files (rc=0). The hosted test has **not** run: it needs the macOS "App build + tests" job on the ready run.
